newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GOLD MEDAL ENDS THE BAD TIMES FOR DIAGANA.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GOLD MEDAL ENDS THE BAD TIMES FOR DIAGANA.

text.p: Stephane Diagana, whose career has been punctuated by a series of injuries, put years of frustration behind him on Monday when he won the world 400 metres hurdles title
The 28-year-old Frenchman, whose Olympic hopes were dashed by a stress fracture to his foot last year, won in 47.70 seconds, the fastest time in the world this year.
Herbert Llewellyn of South Africa, just 20, followed up his silver medal at the world junior championships a year ago with second place here in a lifetime best of 47.86.
American Bryan Bronson, strongly tipped for the gold before the race, had to be content with bronze in 47.88 seconds after losing out in a tremendous tussle with Llewellyn over the last few strides.
Fabrizio Mori of Italy continued to improve, finishing fourth in a personal best of 48.05 seconds, just ahead of 1991 world champion Samuel Matete.
